name: Panel
purpose: A Panel is a plain container that groups other controls so they can be moved, shown, hidden, docked or scrolled together.
whenToUse: Divide a form into regions such as a header, sidebar and content area.
Show or hide a whole group of controls with a single Visible property.
Scroll a large block of controls by setting AutoScroll = true.
realWorldExamples: A sidebar panel docked to the left holding navigation buttons.
A 'page' panel that is swapped with other panels in a wizard.
A custom-drawn control surface built on a Panel.
defaultAppearance: An invisible rectangle that takes the parent's background color, with no border and no caption. Set BorderStyle or BackColor to make it visible.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dropping controls on a Panel in the designer and then moving them to the form by accident.
commonMistakes.fix: Check the Document Outline or Properties window to confirm the parent, or drag the control into the panel.

commonMistakes.mistake: Overlapping several panels and losing track of them.
commonMistakes.fix: Use TableLayoutPanel, or Dock with Fill, and use BringToFront/SendToBack deliberately.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using Panel to group RadioButtons and expecting a caption.
commonMistakes.fix: Use a GroupBox when you want a visible title around the group.

relatedNotes.name: GroupBox
relatedNotes.difference: A container with a visible border and caption text.

relatedNotes.name: FlowLayoutPanel
relatedNotes.difference: Panel that arranges its children automatically in rows or columns.

relatedNotes.name: TableLayoutPanel
relatedNotes.difference: Panel that arranges its children in a grid of rows and columns.

relatedNotes.name: SplitContainer
relatedNotes.difference: Two panels separated by a draggable splitter.

name: GroupBox
purpose: A GroupBox is a container with a border and a caption that visually groups related controls. It also defines the group for RadioButtons placed inside it.
whenToUse: Group related options under a title such as 'Delivery method'.
Create separate sets of RadioButtons on the same form.
Disable a whole section by setting Enabled = false on the GroupBox.
realWorldExamples: A 'Font' group in a settings dialog.
A 'Payment method' box with several radio buttons.
'Filters' and 'Sort by' sections in a search form.
defaultAppearance: A thin etched rectangle with its Text shown as a caption at the top-left, interrupting the border line. Controls inside are positioned relative to the box.

commonMistakes.mistake: Setting Dock = Fill and having the content collide with the caption.
commonMistakes.fix: Put a Panel inside the GroupBox, dock the Panel, and then place the controls in the Panel.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting scroll bars when content does not fit.
commonMistakes.fix: GroupBox does not scroll; use a Panel with AutoScroll inside it, or resize the box.

commonMistakes.mistake: Placing controls on top of the GroupBox in the designer instead of inside it, so disabling or moving the box does not affect them.
commonMistakes.fix: Drag each control into the GroupBox so it becomes a child; check that the Document Outline shows it nested.

relatedNotes.name: Panel
relatedNotes.difference: No border or caption by default, and it can scroll.

relatedNotes.name: TabControl
relatedNotes.difference: Shows several groups, one at a time, on tabs.

relatedNotes.name: RadioButton
relatedNotes.difference: The control most often grouped inside a GroupBox.

name: TabControl
purpose: A TabControl displays several pages, each on its own tab, and shows one page at a time. It organizes a lot of content in a small space.
whenToUse: Split a settings dialog into General, Advanced and About pages.
Show several documents or views in the same area.
Organize a complex form into logical sections.
realWorldExamples: The Options dialog in many applications.
A customer form with Details, Orders and Notes tabs.
A multi-document editor with a tab per file.
defaultAppearance: A row of tab headers across the top (Alignment = Top), with the selected tab joined to a bordered page area below. New tabs are named TabPage1, TabPage2 and so on.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding tabs through the Controls collection and getting nothing.
commonMistakes.fix: Add TabPage objects to the TabPages collection.

commonMistakes.mistake: Reading controls on a tab that has never been shown and finding them empty or unready.
commonMistakes.fix: Initialize data in the form load, or in the TabControl.Selected event, and avoid relying on lazy creation.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using too many tabs to fit.
commonMistakes.fix: Set Multiline = true for several rows, or choose a different layout such as a list on the left.

relatedNotes.name: TabPage
relatedNotes.difference: One page inside a TabControl; the container for that tab's controls.

relatedNotes.name: Panel
relatedNotes.difference: A single group; swap Panels manually for a custom tab-like effect.

relatedNotes.name: GroupBox
relatedNotes.difference: Shows all groups at once instead of one at a time.

name: TabPage
purpose: A TabPage is one page of a TabControl. It is a container that holds the controls shown when its tab is selected.
whenToUse: Define the content of each tab in a TabControl.
Hide or show a tab by adding or removing the page from TabPages.
Give each tab a Text caption and optional icon via ImageIndex.
realWorldExamples: The 'General' page of a settings dialog.
A page per customer in a CRM window.
A 'Preview' page showing the rendered output.
defaultAppearance: A bordered panel that fills the page area of its TabControl. Its Text appears on the tab header, and its background is the system's tab-page color.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to set Visible = false to hide a tab.
commonMistakes.fix: Remove the page from TabControl.TabPages (and add it back later) because Visible does not hide the tab header.

commonMistakes.mistake: Creating a TabPage without adding it to a TabControl and expecting it to display.
commonMistakes.fix: A TabPage can only be shown inside a TabControl; add it to TabPages.

commonMistakes.mistake: Setting Size or Location on a TabPage.
commonMistakes.fix: The TabControl controls the page size; resize the TabControl instead.

relatedNotes.name: TabControl
relatedNotes.difference: The parent that holds the pages and draws the tab headers.

relatedNotes.name: Panel
relatedNotes.difference: A general container that is not tied to a tab control.

name: SplitContainer
purpose: A SplitContainer divides an area into two resizable panels separated by a splitter bar that the user can drag.
whenToUse: Build master/detail layouts such as a list on the left and details on the right.
Let the user decide how much space each region gets.
Nest splitters for a three-pane layout.
realWorldExamples: A file explorer with a folder tree and a file list.
An email client with a folder list, message list and reading pane.
A code editor with a tool window at the bottom.
defaultAppearance: Two equal panels side by side (Orientation = Vertical splitter), divided by a thin movable bar. Each panel, Panel1 and Panel2, is a container for other controls.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding controls to the SplitContainer itself.
commonMistakes.fix: Add them to SplitContainer.Panel1 or Panel2.

commonMistakes.mistake: Setting SplitterDistance too large at startup and getting an exception.
commonMistakes.fix: Set it after the control has its final size, or respect Panel1MinSize and Panel2MinSize.

commonMistakes.mistake: Panels do not resize as expected when the form grows.
commonMistakes.fix: Set FixedPanel to the panel that should keep its size.

relatedNotes.name: Panel
relatedNotes.difference: A single container with no splitter.

relatedNotes.name: TableLayoutPanel
relatedNotes.difference: A grid whose size is fixed by styles; users cannot drag the dividers.

relatedNotes.name: TabControl
relatedNotes.difference: Shows several pages in one area instead of side by side.

name: FlowLayoutPanel
purpose: A FlowLayoutPanel arranges its child controls one after another in a row or a column, wrapping to the next line when it runs out of space.
whenToUse: Show a list of buttons, tags or cards that should wrap.
Build a form of controls that appear or disappear dynamically.
Avoid manual positioning of many similar controls.
realWorldExamples: A toolbar-like row of buttons that wraps on narrow windows.
A gallery of thumbnails.
A set of filter 'chips' that the user can add and remove.
defaultAppearance: An invisible container (no border by default) in which controls are placed left to right in the order they were added (FlowDirection = LeftToRight). With WrapContents = true they continue on a new row.

commonMistakes.mistake: Setting Location on children and seeing it ignored.
commonMistakes.fix: The panel decides positions; use the child's Margin to control spacing.

commonMistakes.mistake: Wrong order of controls.
commonMistakes.fix: Order follows the Controls collection; change it with SetChildIndex or by adding in the correct order.

commonMistakes.mistake: Children do not fill the width.
commonMistakes.fix: Set the child's Anchor, or set FlowDirection = TopDown with WrapContents = false and use Anchor Left, Right.

relatedNotes.name: TableLayoutPanel
relatedNotes.difference: Places controls into fixed cells of a grid, not in a flowing sequence.

relatedNotes.name: Panel
relatedNotes.difference: Places controls exactly where you put them.

name: TableLayoutPanel
purpose: A TableLayoutPanel arranges its children in a grid of rows and columns, so complex forms line up and resize correctly.
whenToUse: Build forms where labels and inputs must stay aligned.
Create responsive layouts using percentage-based rows and columns.
Place several controls in a dialog without manual coordinates.
realWorldExamples: A data entry form with labels in column one and text boxes in column two.
A dashboard split into equal tiles.
A settings page with aligned label/value pairs.
defaultAppearance: An invisible grid of two equal rows and columns by default, with no lines (CellBorderStyle = None). Each cell holds one control, which you can make span cells with ColumnSpan or RowSpan.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dropping several controls into the same cell.
commonMistakes.fix: Only one control belongs in a cell; use a Panel or another TableLayoutPanel when a cell needs several.

commonMistakes.mistake: Child controls not filling their cell.
commonMistakes.fix: Set Dock = Fill, or set Anchor to all sides, and check the Margin.

commonMistakes.mistake: Deep nesting that makes the form slow and hard to read.
commonMistakes.fix: Use one table with ColumnSpan/RowSpan where possible, and keep nesting shallow.

relatedNotes.name: FlowLayoutPanel
relatedNotes.difference: Places controls one after another and wraps; no fixed cells.

relatedNotes.name: Panel
relatedNotes.difference: Absolute positioning by Location instead of a grid.

relatedNotes.name: SplitContainer
relatedNotes.difference: Two areas whose boundary the user can drag.
